endorsements.quote: Prospective, multicentre studies incorporating patient-reported outcomes and lesion-specific predictors (eg, Eisenmenger physiology, Fontan-associated liver disease markers) are urgently needed.
Future clinical practice should embed AI models within clinical workflows, ensuring human oversight, interpretability and the ability to adapt dynamically as patient conditions evolve.

unlisted_practices: Validate AI and wearable technologies prospectively in the specific patient populations where they will be used, such as congenital heart disease populations.
Validate wearable devices against gold-standard diagnostic tools, incorporating signal quality analyses.
Design AI-driven triage alerts with clear thresholds for action to avoid overburdening clinicians with false-positive alerts.
Define eligibility criteria and escalation triggers for hybrid telemedicine and in-person care pathways.
Keep responsibility for managing complex cases with specialists and use digital health to complement rather than replace expert oversight.
Embed privacy safeguards and cybersecurity into digital infrastructure from the outset.
Use federated learning and privacy-preserving analytics to share sensitive patient data safely.
Co-design patient education and engagement tools with patients, prioritising digital inclusivity and cultural sensitivity.
Provide clinician training and reimbursement strategies so digital care models are sustainable.
Address socioeconomic barriers to digital access through public-private partnerships and policy.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary discussing current developments and future priorities/governance frameworks for digital health technologies and AI in adult congenital heart disease care.
